status_note: active; @ark-ui/react|vue|solid 5.39.2 and @ark-ui/svelte 5.24.2 released 2026-09-13 on Zag 1.44.0; 15 open issues
core_problem: Provide one accessible, headless behaviour implementation per widget (accordion, tabs, carousel, dialog, menu, combobox, ...) that works identically in React, Vue, Solid and Svelte by moving all logic into framework-agnostic Zag.js state machines and keeping the framework layer to prop plumbing.
architecture: Two repos. chakra-ui/zag holds the logic: `@zag-js/core` (create-machine.ts, types.ts) defines a machine as `{ props(), initialState(), context() of bindable values, computed, refs, watch(track), on, states: { <state>: { entry, exit, effects, on: { EVENT: Transition | Transition[] } } }, implementations: { guards, actions, effects } }` with `createGuards()` (and/or/not) and string-keyed actions/guards so the machine is declarative data. Each widget lives in `packages/machines/<name>/src/` as five files: `<name>.machine.ts` (states/transitions, e.g. accordion has `idle` and `focused` with events TRIGGER.FOCUS/BLUR/CLICK, GOTO.NEXT/PREV/FIRST/LAST, VALUE.SET and guards `isExpanded`, `canToggle`), `<name>.connect.ts` (pure function `connect(service, normalizeProps)` that projects state into per-part prop bags: `getRootProps/getItemProps/getItemTriggerProps/getItemContentProps/getItemIndicatorProps` emitting `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`, `hidden`, `data-state=open|closed`, `data-orientation`, `data-focus`, `data-disabled`, plus keyboard maps ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right/Home/End via `getEventKey` with dir/orientation awareness), `<name>.anatomy.ts` (`createAnatomy('accordion').parts('root','item','itemTrigger','itemContent','itemIndicator')` producing `data-scope`/`data-part` attributes), `<name>.dom.ts` (id scheme and element queries through a `Scope` with getRootNode for shadow DOM) and `<name>.types.ts`. The framework adapters in `packages/frameworks/{react,vue,solid,svelte,preact,vanilla}` each implement the same `useMachine` interpreter (react/src/machine.ts uses useRef/flushSync/useSyncExternalStore; svelte/src/machine.svelte.ts uses $derived/$effect runes; vanilla/src/machine.ts is a `VanillaMachine` class with `subscribe`, `send`, `updateProps`, `start/stop`) plus `normalizeProps` (framework prop naming) and, for vanilla, `spreadProps(node, attrs, machineId)` which diff-applies attributes, inline styles (property by property so popper `--x/--y` vars survive) and event listeners onto existing DOM nodes. Carousel machine (carousel.machine.ts, 582 lines) is built on native CSS scroll-snap (`@zag-js/scroll-snap` computes snap positions, `scrollSnapType` set in connect), has `idle`/`dragging`/`autoplay` states, IntersectionObserver-tracked `slidesInView` (inViewThreshold 0.6), ResizeObserver, pauses autoplay on `visibilitychange`, and connect emits `role=region` + `aria-roledescription=carousel`, `aria-live` polite/off depending on autoplay, slides as `role=group aria-roledescription=slide` with `aria-hidden` when out of view, prev/next `aria-controls`, and an autoplay toggle with start/stop labels. chakra-ui/ark is the thin component layer: `packages/react/src/components/accordion/use-accordion.ts` is 15 lines (`useMachine(accordion.machine, {id, dir, getRootNode, ...props})` then `accordion.connect(service, normalizeProps)`), `accordion-root.tsx` splits machine props from DOM props with `createSplitProps`, merges `getRootProps()` via `mergeProps` and renders `ark.div` (polymorphic factory with `asChild`); `accordion-item-content.tsx` delegates to `Collapsible.Content`, whose `use-presence.ts` wraps `@zag-js/presence` for animation-aware mount/unmount with `lazyMount`, `unmountOnExit`, `hideMode: 'display-none' | 'activity'` (React Activity when supported) and `skipAnimationOnMount`. The Svelte layer (`packages/svelte/src/lib/components/accordion/accordion-root.svelte`, `use-accordion.svelte.ts`) is the same shape with `$bindable` value and `$derived` props, confirming that ~95% of behaviour is in Zag. Extension points: `EnvironmentProvider` (root node), `LocaleProvider` (dir), `ids` overrides, `translations` per machine, `data-scope/data-part` for styling recipes (Park UI). Bundle (esm.sh bundled, gzip): @zag-js/vanilla 6.7 kB, @zag-js/accordion 3.3 kB, @zag-js/tabs 6.5 kB, @zag-js/carousel 9.8 kB, @zag-js/collapsible 4.4 kB, @zag-js/presence 2.5 kB, @zag-js/dom-query 11.2 kB (shared, partially tree-shaken per machine), @zag-js/react 4.4 kB + React; @ark-ui/react full barrel 290 kB gz with 69 deps (not tree-shake-safe: sideEffects false is not set).
core_innovation: One declarative state machine plus one pure connect() projection per widget serves every framework, including vanilla DOM, so accessibility semantics and keyboard behaviour are written once as data and the framework adapter is only an interpreter plus prop normaliser.
strengths: Framework-free path exists and is real: `@zag-js/vanilla` (VanillaMachine + spreadProps + normalizeProps) can run an accordion/tabs/carousel machine against server-rendered Astro HTML with no React/Vue/Svelte runtime, ~10-17 kB gz per widget including core.

A11y is baked into connect(): role/aria-* wiring, `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby` id contracts, orientation- and RTL-aware key maps, `hidden` on collapsed panels, `aria-roledescription` carousel/slide, `aria-live` handling, autoplay pause on document hidden.
Machine spec is declarative and inspectable: states, events, guards, actions are strings resolved in `implementations`, so the behaviour graph can be validated, tested, or even snapshotted as data.
Anatomy contract (`data-scope`, `data-part`, `data-state`) decouples styling completely from behaviour; CSS can target parts without classes.
Carousel is built on native CSS scroll-snap rather than transform math, so it degrades to a plain scrollable list without JS and respects browser scroll physics.
Presence machine handles enter/exit animation waits (animationend) generically, with lazy mount / unmount-on-exit / display-none vs Activity hide modes.
Large surface (60+ machines) with monthly releases across four frameworks; MIT.
weaknesses: Zag machines run entirely client-side and require the DOM ids/attributes to be applied by the adapter; with SSR'd Astro HTML you must either pre-render the exact same attribute set (ids, aria, data-state) or accept a hydration flash while spreadProps rewrites them.

Per-widget cost is not trivial relative to native HTML: an accordion via vanilla Zag is ~10 kB gz where `<details name>` with a few lines of CSS is 0 kB; tabs ~13 kB; carousel ~17 kB. Fine within 180 kB, but each island adds up.
Full `@ark-ui/react` is 290 kB gz / 69 deps and does not declare `sideEffects: false`; only per-machine `@zag-js/*` imports are budget-safe.
The vanilla adapter has no docs beyond source (README missing), only a jsdom test suite; API stability of `spreadProps`/`VanillaMachine` is less proven than the React/Vue adapters.
Machines do not read `prefers-reduced-motion`: carousel autoplay and presence animations are left to CSS; the caller must gate autoplay and keyframes.
Some machines pull heavy shared utilities (`dom-query` 11 kB, `interact-outside`, `focus-visible`) into dialog/menu/popover, so overlays cost 20-30 kB gz even in vanilla.
Maintained by a small team (Segun Adebayo's Chakra org); breaking changes between Zag majors (v0 -> v1 rewrote the machine API in 2025).
patterns_to_steal: Machine-per-widget as declarative data (`states`, `on`, `guards`, `actions` as string keys resolved in `implementations`) → section variant `a11y` contract: express each interactive section's allowed states/events (accordion: idle/focused; carousel: idle/dragging/autoplay) so the QA gate can assert keyboard paths from the spec, not from prose.

connect() prop-bag projection with anatomy parts (`data-scope`, `data-part`, `data-state`, `data-orientation`) → renderer: Astro section templates render exactly these attributes server-side so styling and Playwright/axe assertions target parts, and a vanilla machine can attach without rewriting markup.

`@zag-js/vanilla` VanillaMachine + spreadProps on existing DOM → islands runtime: for FAQ accordion, feature tabs and testimonial carousel, hydrate SSR'd HTML with the machine (10-17 kB gz each) instead of shipping a framework island; keep native `<details>` for the cheapest accordion arrangements.

Carousel on CSS scroll-snap with IntersectionObserver `slidesInView`, `aria-roledescription`, autoplay pause on `visibilitychange` → testimonial/logo carousel arrangements: base markup must scroll-snap natively (JS-off fallback), autoplay only when eligibility allows and never under reduced motion.
Presence machine's animationend-aware unmount with lazyMount/unmountOnExit → motion layer: reuse for any expand/collapse so exit animations complete before `hidden` is applied.

Id scheme through a `Scope` (`getById`, `getRootNode`) with overridable `ids` → SiteDefinition: assign deterministic section-scoped ids at assembly time so aria-controls/labelledby pairs are stable across rebuilds and diffable.
patterns_to_avoid: Importing `@ark-ui/react` (or vue/solid/svelte) into Astro islands → framework runtime per island plus a 290 kB gz barrel with 69 deps; use `@zag-js/<machine>` + `@zag-js/vanilla` directly, or native HTML.

Using Zag for content that native HTML already handles (single-open accordion via `<details name>`, simple disclosure, static tabs that can be links) → 0 kB beats 10 kB; reserve machines for roving-focus tabs, carousels with autoplay/indicators, and overlays.
Relying on the machines for reduced-motion or motion budget → they do not consult `prefers-reduced-motion`; motion gating must live in our token CSS and in the section's `motion` budget.

Overlay machines (dialog, menu, popover, combobox) in marketing sections → 20-30 kB gz each with focus-trap/interact-outside/dom-query; marketing pages should avoid overlays except a single mobile nav drawer, which native `<dialog>` covers.
Client-only attribute application (letting spreadProps add aria/ids after hydration) → hydration flash and axe failures on the SSR snapshot; render the connect() attribute set at build time.
reusable_patterns: DeclarativeWidgetMachine: widget behaviour as a serialisable state chart with string-keyed guards/actions and separate implementations.
ConnectProjection: a pure function from machine state to per-part attribute/handler bags, framework-agnostic via a normalizeProps shim.
AnatomyPartsContract: `data-scope`/`data-part`/`data-state` attributes as the only coupling between behaviour and styling.
VanillaHydrateExistingDOM: attach a machine to server-rendered markup by diff-spreading attributes, styles and listeners rather than re-rendering.
ScrollSnapCarousel: native scroll-snap as the base with JS only for indicators, autoplay and aria-live.
AnimationAwarePresence: wait for animationend before hiding/unmounting, with lazy mount and unmount-on-exit options.
adoption_strategy: Adapt (Adopt the Zag machines selectively, not Ark). Yes, state-machine-per-widget is the right a11y base for interactive sections, but consume it as `@zag-js/accordion|tabs|carousel` + `@zag-js/vanilla` inside Astro `<script>` islands attached to SSR'd markup, never as an Ark framework island. Encode the connect() attribute set (role, aria-*, data-part, data-state, ids) into the Astro section templates at build time so the static HTML already passes axe and the machine only takes over interactivity; budget roughly 10 kB gz for accordion, 13 kB tabs, 17 kB carousel and prefer native `<details>`/scroll-snap-only arrangements when the variant's `motion`/`a11y` spec allows. Reuse the machine vocabulary (states, events, guards) as the schema for our section `a11y` contract, and gate carousel autoplay and presence animations with our reduced-motion tokens since Zag does not.
